summary: Shih Hu worked in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cornell, Columbia under John Dewey, and under Kaiten Nukariya. He served as chancellor of Peking University (1946–1948) and president of Academia Sinica (1957–1962).
Shih-Hsiang Chen was a sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1932–1936). He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1945–1971) and taught Gary Snyder.

Shili Xiong was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at the China Institute of Inner Learning under Jian Ouyang in 1920. He held posts at Peking University (1923–1955) and Zhejiang University (~1937–1940).
Shimin Geng specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China (~1949–1952) and later held a post there (~1953).

Shin Fujinaga is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Hiroshima University (attested 1992) and at the National Institute of Technology, Miyakonojo College, where he was an associate professor (attested 2000).

Shin'ichi Chigusa specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University (~1974–1980), where he later served as an assistant (~1980–1984), before holding a post at Yamagata University (~1984).

Shin'ichi Hisamatsu was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida and Shozan Ikegami. He was a professor at Hanazono (1919), Ryukoku (1929), and Kyoto University (1935–1953).
Shindai Sekiguchi worked in Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1928–1934), he served as a professor at Taisho University (~1960–1978) and at Hanazono University (~1978–1982).

Shingen Takagi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University under Gisho Nakano, Yusho Miyasaka, Ensho Kanakura, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as assistant professor (attested 1970) and president (attested 1991–1995) at Koyasan University.

Shingo Einoo is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau (~1976–1980) and held a post at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~1989–2013).
Shingo Enomoto is an Indologist and linguist who completed a PhD at the University of Marburg (~1976–1980). He served as an assistant at the National Museum of Ethnology (~1980–1989).

Shinichi Nakazawa works in religious studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1969–1977) and held positions at Chuo University (~1993–2006), Tama Art University (~2006–2011), and Meiji University (~2011).

Shinichi Tsuda works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later teaching at the Eastern Institute and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1993). He held a post at Tottori University (~1995–2000) and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2012).

Shinjo Hinonishi worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology, having studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held posts at Koyasan University as assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar who studied under Hajime Nakamura and Dale Riepe. He taught as a Fulbright lecturer at Buffalo (~1967–1968) and as professor at the University of Tsukuba (1986–1997).

Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra and served as professor at Rissho University (~1970–1996).

Shinjosei Mochizuki was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923) and Kyoto University (~1923–1926), and held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.

Shinkai Sugahara specialized in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1948–1951) and Taisho University (-1991), and served as professor emeritus at Waseda University (-1972).

Shinkan Murakami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Nobuo Kumagai, and Ryūjō Yamada, later serving there as professor (~1979–1996) and professor emeritus (~1996).
